videos.title: At the Gate
videos.description: Placeholder for the ODIN pipeline, not a finished recording. A slow moss gradient, a little noise, and a low drone. Hávamál stanza 1, in the 1923 translation by Henry Adams Bellows, stays on screen the whole time.
videos.subtitleCitation: Henry Adams Bellows, translator. Hovamol. The Poetic Edda. New York: The American-Scandinavian Foundation, 1923. Public domain.
videos.subtitleText:
Within the gates | ere a man shall go,
(Full warily let him watch,)
Full long let him look about him;
For little he knows | where a foe may lurk,
And sit in the seats within.

videos.title: The Road Alone
videos.description: Placeholder. Dusk colours drift across the frame under a soft chord. Hávamál 47, Bellows 1923, held for the full length of the clip.
videos.subtitleCitation: Henry Adams Bellows, translator. Hovamol. The Poetic Edda. New York: The American-Scandinavian Foundation, 1923. Public domain.
videos.subtitleText:
Young was I once, | and wandered alone,
And nought of the road I knew;
Rich did I feel | when a comrade I found,
For man is man's delight.

videos.title: A Name That Stays
videos.description: Placeholder. Night colours and a quiet low chord. Hávamál 77, Bellows 1923: the stanza about a name that outlasts cattle and kin.
videos.subtitleCitation: Henry Adams Bellows, translator. Hovamol. The Poetic Edda. New York: The American-Scandinavian Foundation, 1923. Public domain.
videos.subtitleText:
Cattle die, | and kinsmen die,
And so one dies one's self;
But a noble name | will never die,
If good renown one gets.
